correctness.rationale: Fresh exhaustive replay over all anonymous strict three-candidate profiles found zero Bucklin no-show events for electorates of size at most five and exactly 18 bad profiles at six voters. All 18 events use a single abstainer. Normalizing the abstainer to rank A>B>C gives exactly the three profiles (1,t,0,3,2-t,0) for t=0,1,2; candidate relabeling gives three orbits of size six. There are 462 anonymous six-voter profiles and 417 with unique Bucklin winner, so the two exact incidences are 3/77 and 6/139.
residual_risks: Different tie-breaking or nonanonymous Bucklin conventions are outside scope.

originality.rationale: Brandt, Matthäus and Saile already prove that the Bucklin No-Show Paradox first appears with three candidates and six voters, so the minimum itself is prior art. Their full article and summary table do not state the complete anonymous six-voter census, its 18 profiles, the three relabeling classes, or the exact incidence fractions. Targeted Resultary and web searches found no prior equivalent boundary classification.
